articles.description: Actor Nana Patekar was declared dead after being brought to Manipal Hospital in Goa. He sent a message to a friend indicating he was unwell before losing consciousness. Friends and a caretaker accompanied him when he was taken to the hospital. Medical staff attempted to revive him for nearly an hour but declared him dead upon arrival. His body has been sent for a post-mortem examination following a medico-legal case.

articles.title: Coastal Forest Loss Speeds Up: Albemarle Peninsula trees retreat 21%; ghost forests spread faster
articles.description: Over the last 36 years, North Carolina's coastal forests have seen a dramatic decrease in forest cover. The decline sped up after 2010 due to rising sea levels and increased salinity. The research revealed a troubling shift, with once green areas transforming into marshes, shrubs, or ghost forests. Moreover, extreme weather events have intensified the threat of saltwater intrusion, making these forests increasingly vulnerable.

articles.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex plunges over 750 points, NSE Nifty50 slips below 22,400
articles.full_text: The key overhang is no longer the RBI’s rate increase alone, but the growing prospect of tighter domestic and global monetary conditions persisting for longer, potentially keeping pressure on risk appetite and foreign flows. The RBI’s shift to calibrated tightening, followed by Federal Reserve minutes indicating another US rate increase may be required this year, could limit risk appetite The outlook for Indian equities remains cautious after the RBI raised its repo rate to 5.50 per cent, tightening domestic financial conditions at a time when global markets are already contending with elevated Treasury yields and geopolitical uncertainty. Tighter domestic financial conditions and a fragile global risk backdrop could keep investors defensive Stock market today: Top stock recommendations for October 8 Dalal Street is expected to open slightly lower after the previous session’s decline, with the RBI’s rate decision and rising oil prices remaining key factors in the market backdrop. GIFT Nifty futures were at 22,600.5, indicating a weaker start for the Nifty 50, which had closed at 22,603.05 in the previous session. The RBI had raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% and changed its stance from “neutral” to “calibrated tightening”. The move came amid higher inflation concerns linked to rising oil prices. Investors were also set to track Tata Consultancy Services as it began the September-quarter earnings season for large companies. Foreign investors had sold Rs 6,121.37 crore of Indian shares in the previous session, according to provisional data. Rupee weakened 40 paise to close at 96.75 against the US dollar after the RBI raised the benchmark policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%. The currency opened at 96.37 and traded in a range of 96.34-96.84 before settling at 96.75, compared with its previous close of 96.35. The dollar index was trading at 102.28, up 0.45%. According to Dilip Parmar, senior research analyst at HDFC Securities, the rupee recorded its second-weakest close and trailed most Asian peers following the RBI’s hawkish note and renewed inflation concerns. Parmar said a rebound in crude oil prices and risk aversion added pressure on the currency. He identified 96.97 as resistance for USD-INR, with support at 96.30. BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 ended Wednesday on a lower note, after two straight sessions of gains, with the RBI’s 25-basis-point repo rate increase and its shift to a “calibrated tightening” stance weighing on sentiment. The 30-share BSE Sensex fell 429.11 points, or 0.59%, to 72,638.70, with 26 constituents closing lower and four higher. The index had declined as much as 599.09 points, or 0.81%, to 72,468.72 during the session. The NSE Nifty declined 173.05 points, or 0.76%, to 22,603.05. Rising crude oil prices and persistent foreign fund outflows also affected sentiment. Among Sensex stocks, Titan, Bharat Electronics, Asian Paints, Infosys, Larsen & Toubro and Adani Ports were among the major laggards, while Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bharti Airtel, ICICI Bank and Bajaj Finance gained.

articles.title: Nana Patekar passes away: Last rites to be held at actor's farmhouse
articles.full_text: Superstar Rajinikanth expressed shock at the death of veteran star Nana Patekar, saying he couldn't believe his “dear friend” was “no longer with us.” Remembering the late actor, Rajinikanth took to X and offered his condolences and prayed for his soul to rest in peace. “I can’t believe my dear friend Nanaji is no longer with us. My deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. May his soul rest in peace,” Rajinikanth tweeted. Rajinikanth and Nana Patekar have together worked in the 2018 film Kaala, an action drama film directed and co-written by Pa. Ranjith. . The film stars Rajinikanth in the titular role, alongside Nana Patekar, Eswari Rao, Huma Qureshi Samuthirakani, Pankaj Tripathi, Anjali Patil, K. Manikandan, Dileepan, Nitish Veera, Sampath Raj and Ravi Kale. The film follows Karikalan "Kaala", the leader of Dharavi, who tries to save his land from getting seized and his people from being evicted by Haridev, a ruthless minister. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan on Thursday expressed grief over the passing of veteran actor Nana Patekar and extended condolences to his family members. Nana Patekar, one of Indian cinema's most celebrated performers, passed away at the age of 75 in Goa. An official confirmation from Manipal Hospital, Goa, stated that the actor was found unconscious at his Dona Paula -- Goa residence -- and was rushed to the hospital. Doctors declared him brought dead. Taking to X, President Murmu said, "Deeply saddened by the passing of veteran actor Shri Nana Patekar. Through his powerful and deeply evocative performances, he brought to life a wide range of human experiences." "He portrayed characters that left a lasting imprint on the hearts and minds of people. His commitment to social service reflected his concern for the underprivileged. His passing is a great loss to Indian cinema. I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family and admirers," the President added. Vice President Radhakrishnan also said that he was "deeply saddened" by the passing of the veteran actor. "A versatile and immensely talented artist, he brought remarkable depth, sensitivity and authenticity to every character he portrayed. His invaluable contribution to Indian cinema will always be remembered. Known for his powerful performances, Nana Patekar Ji will continue to inspire and be cherished by generations of cinema lovers," the Vice President said in a post on X. "In this hour of grief, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and countless admirers," he added. The demise of veteran actor Nana Patekar has left the film industry mourning the loss of one of the industry's finest stars. Actor Sunny Deol paid an emotional tribute to Patekar, remembering him as a “fearless” and “full of life” person and recalling the special bond they shared over the years. Sharing a picture with Nana Patekar on his social media account, Sunny Deol wrote, “Still can’t believe Nana is not among us. We never worked together, but we always shared a very special bond that went back many years. Fearless, full of life, he always did what he wanted to do. That’s how I’ll always remember him. Will miss you, Nana.” The picture shared by Sunny features the two veteran actors posing together with their arms around each other. The picture appears to have been taken at an event connected to Gadar 2, with the film’s title visible in the backdrop. Actor-filmmaker Farhan Akhtar remembered veteran actor Nana Patekar as a “generational talent” who could command attention with his mere presence, saying his contributions to the arts and social causes will remain an inspiration. Farhan, whose father, Javed Akhtar, wrote the song lyrics for Nana Patekar's 1998 romantic thriller film Wajood, took to Instagram and shared a picture of the late legendary star. He wrote in the caption: “There are some who leave a void in their absence. Nana Patekar was one such person, whose presence could fill up a room and he was a generational talent who commanded our attention when on screen.” “His work in the arts and his commitment to social causes remain an inspiration to us all.RIP You will be missed sir but never forgotten.” Veteran actor Nana Patekar, one of the country's most notable stars, passed away at his Goa residence in the early hours of Thursday morning, at age 75. An official confirmation from the Manipal Hospital, Goa, stated that the actor was found unconscious at his Dona Paula, residence and was rushed to the hospital. In a video statement to the media, Dr Shekhar Salkar shared the details about the actor's final moments. Recalling the events of the night, Dr Salkar shared, "Nana Patekar was brought dead to the hospital, somewhere around 4.30 am and was declared dead by 5.30 am. We had tried our best to save him, but he was brought dead. Cardiac massage was given for almost 45 minutes to 1 hour, but he just could not be saved." He also confirmed that a formal police case has been registered and confirmed, "The body has now been taken to the morgue in Goa Medical College for postmortem." In a statement to PTI, he shared that investigation into the cause of death is on. He said, "It was a cardiac arrest, but we do not know the cause. He was a known cardiac patient and was on medication, as far as we have been told." "NANA PATEKAR THE GREATEST?💔💔A couple of hours ago, I received the heartbreaking news that my friend Nana Patekar, one of the finest actors and human beings in Indian cinema, is no more.🥹🥹🥹 I had just finished our performance and taken the curtain call. As I walked into the wings, my director Gajendra told me, “Nana is no more.”🥹 After that, I had to meet people, pose for photographs, smile, sit down for a meal… while trying to absorb what I had just heard. It was terribly difficult. But somewhere, I felt that Nana would have wanted me to finish my work. Fulfil my responsibility to the people who had come to see us. And then, perhaps, remember him. Actually, knowing him, I can almost hear him dismissing the very idea of a tribute: “अरे, तो क्या हो गया? मर गया तो कौन-सी बड़ी बात है? सभी मरते हैं!” That was Nana. Direct, unpretentious, with his own way of saying even the most difficult things.❤️‍🩹 I will miss you, my friend. Your warmth. Your hugs. Your extraordinary performances. And whenever I miss seeing you, I will watch your films. Though today, I wish I could simply hug you one more time. My love and deepest condolences to your family and to everyone who loved you. अलविदा मेरे दोस्त, नाना पाटेकर। बहुत सारा प्यार।," wrote Anupam Kher. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath mourned Nana Patekar's death and remembered his contribution to cinema and society. "The demise of the renowned actor, powerful theatre artist, and sensitive social worker, Padma Shri Nana Patekar ji, is an irreplaceable loss to the world of art. Through his exceptional acting, he enriched Indian cinema and also expressed his commitment to society through his social concerns. May Lord Shri Ram grant a place at His divine feet to the departed soul and provide strength to the grieving family and admirers to bear this sorrow. Just three days before his untimely passing, Nana Patekar had stood before an audience at a social event in Goa and, with his characteristic style, remarked that everyone has to go someday and "I don’t know whether I will be here tomorrow.” Patekar was addressing a function of Samraat Club International at Dona Paula near Panaji in Goa on October 4, during which he also remembered his friend and former Goa chief minister, late Manohar Parrikar. "We all have to go someday. I don't know whether I will be here tomorrow. That time comes in the life of everyone. But before that time comes (we have to think, whether), am I able to do what I want to do? Have I made the effort?," Patekar said. The 76-year-old actor passed away in Goa early on Thursday. He is suspected to have suffered a heart attack. The body was shifted to the Goa Medical College and Hospital near Panaji for postmortem. On Sunday, addressing the gathering at Dona Paula, Patekar remembered former CM Parrikar as his friend. "Parrikar was a person about whom one could be proud. He was younger than me. I am now 76, and will turn 77. But he was such a great person that one had to look up to him," the actor said. "We are fortunate that such a person was born here. These are people who lived their lives as if they had taken up a mission," he noted. Veteran actor Nana Patekar, one of the country's most notable stars, passed away at his Goa residence in the early hours of Thursday morning, at age 75. Maharashtra Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar on Thursday announced that veteran actor Nana Patekar will be accorded a state funeral in recognition of his contribution to theatre and cinema. The Devendra Fadnavis government took the decision considering Patekar's unparalleled contribution to the fields of Marathi theatre and Marathi and Hindi cinema, Shelar said. Patekar was a recipient of three National Film Awards, several Filmfare Awards, the Maharashtra State Film Award and Filmfare Awards Marathi. He had also received Padma Shri, the country's fourth-highest civilian honour. Several celebrities from South India including actors Jr NTR and Prabhu Deva joined joined scores of people from across the country in paying rich tributes to veteran actor Nana Patekar, whose sudden demise in Goa on Thursday left the entire nation shocked. Taking to his social media timelines, Telugu star Jr NTR, in his condolence message, wrote, "Deeply saddened by the passing of Nana Patekar sir, one of Indian cinema’s finest actors. There was an unmistakable honesty and intensity in every character he portrayed. His performances never felt like acting, but life unfolding on screen. A remarkable artist whose contribution to Indian cinema will be remembered for generations. Heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones. Om Shanti" Actor and director Prabhu Deva too was among those who expressed grief. On his X timeline, Prabhu Deva said, " Deeply saddened by the passing of the legendary actor Nana Patekar Sir. His powerful performances, remarkable talent and immense contribution to Indian cinema will always be remembered. Heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and admirers." Earlier in the day, actor Prakash Raj wrote, "Miss you my dear Nana ji... Will cherish the moments spent...conversations... arguments... the food you cooked...knowledge you shared. Thank you for coming into my life’s journey. RIP #nanapatekar." Actress and producer Khushbu Sundar too expressed shock and grief at the demise of the acting stalwart. She wrote, "This is unbelievably shocking. I am numb. Devastated infact. An actor par excellence. A man with his own mind and beliefs. A simple hearted human. An actor par excellence. Had the privilege and honor to work with him. You will be missed Nana Bhau. #OmShanti #nanapatekar." The actor expressed grief over the sudden demise of veteran star Nana Patekar, describing him as one of the great artists of Indian cinema and recalling his simplicity, humility and down-to-earth personality. Actor-politician Ravi Kishan expressed grief over the sudden demise of veteran star Nana Patekar, describing him as one of the great artists of Indian cinema and recalling his simplicity, humility and down-to-earth personality. Ravi took to Instagram, where he shared a picture of Nana Patekar and said that his passing was a “deeply personal loss” for him and an “irreparable loss” to the Indian film industry. Ravi took to the caption section and wrote in Hindi, which translated to: “I was deeply saddened to hear the extremely tragic news of Nana Patekar Ji’s passing early this morning. Despite being a star, Nana Ji was always far removed from the trappings of stardom.” The actor-politician said that he was was “one of the great artists of Indian cinema, known for his simplicity, humility and his down-to-earth personality.” “Even while living amidst the glitz and glamour of Mumbai, he never lost touch with his roots and values. I shared a close and warm relationship with Nana Ji. We would speak from time to time, and I learned a great deal from his acting, simplicity and perspective on life.” Ravi shared that Nana always extended his affection and encouragement. “His passing is a deeply personal loss for me as well. Nana Patekar Ji’s demise is an irreparable loss to the Indian film industry. His art, simplicity and memories will always live on among us. May God grant the departed soul a place at His feet and give his family and all those who loved him the strength to bear this immense loss. Om Shanti.” Bollywood superstar Akshay Kumar has expressed grief on the sudden passing of veteran star Nana Patekar, with whom he has worked in iconic comedies such as “Welcome” and “Housefull 5”. Calling him “one of a kind”, Akshay remembered Nana, who passed away on Thursday aged 75 at his home in Goa, for his distinctive voice, intensity and honesty in every performance. Dr Shekhar Salkar said the emergency team reached the actor and started cardiac massage because he was completely unresponsive. "When our ER team went there, they started cardiac massage because he was totally unresponsive." Nana Patekar was subsequently shifted to Manipal Hospital at around 4:20 or 4:30 am. Born Vishwanath Patekar on January 1, 1951, in Maharashtra, Nana Patekar established himself as an actor known for his intensity, dialogue delivery and ability to portray complex and unconventional characters. For the uninitiated, he made his Hindi film debut with Gaman in 1978 and went on to become one of the most respected performers of his generation. Nana’s breakthrough came with films such as Salaam Bombay! and Parinda. He went on to deliver powerpack performances in films including Angaar, Tirangaa, Krantiveer, Agni Sakshi, Khamoshi: The Musical, Yeshwant, Ab Tak Chhappan, Apaharan and Raajneeti. The legendary actor was equally recognised for his work in Marathi cinema and theatre. He also ventured into filmmaking and made his directorial debut with Prahaar: The Final Attack in 1991. His comic performance as Uday Shetty in the Welcome franchise went on to become a rage, especially amongst the younger generation of audiences. Among his other notable films are Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman, Wajood, Hu Tu Tu, Gang, Deewangee, Bhoot, Welcome, Welcome Back, Natsamrat and The Vaccine War, among several others.

articles.full_text: Nana Patekar, a well-known veteran actor, died at his home in Goa in the early hours of Thursday. He was declared dead shortly after being brought to Manipal Hospital by his friends and caretaker. The actor had sent a message to a friend indicating he was feeling unwell before losing consciousness. Cardiac massage was performed for nearly an hour, but unfortunately, he could not be saved.
